exercise1.prompt: Separators, headers and the arguments you reach for on a real file.

files.scores.tsv:
name	score
a	1
b	2
c	3
d	4

exercise1.hint: Without sep="\t" the whole line lands in one column and you get one column and three rows -- the row count would look right and the table would be wrong. len(df) or df.shape[0] counts the rows.

questions.prompt: What happens if you read a tab separated file without sep="\t"?
choices: One very wide column holding the whole line
questions.explain: pandas splits on commas and finds none, so each line becomes a single value. shape tells you immediately: one column where you expected several.

choices: Stops the first row being used as column names
questions.explain: Without it, a file that has no header loses its first row of data to the column names, quietly.

questions.prompt: How do you check the separator was right?
choices: Look at df.shape and the column names
questions.explain: One column where you expected five is the signature of a wrong separator, and shape shows it in one line.
